condition_specific: bladder, blood, brain, breast, cervical, esophageal, intestinal, kidney, lymphatic, lung, prostate, rectum, respiratory tract, skin, testicular, thyroid cancer; leukemia; multiple myeloma; non-Hodgkin's lymphoma
notes: NOTE: Georgia has no workers' compensation presumption for this condition. Cancer coverage (§ 25-3-23) is an employer insurance mandate; cardiovascular coverage (§ 45-9-85) is the State Indemnification Fund lump-sum disability/death benefit; PTSD coverage (§§ 45-25-1 et seq.) is a mandatory employer-funded insurance benefit. None is a WC presumption shifting the burden of proof. Requires 12 consecutive months of service as a firefighter with the same fire department. Provides mandatory insurance coverage (lump sum + monthly disability benefit) rather than a direct WC presumption. Effective January 1, 2018. Volunteers covered under same statute but with lower benefit levels ($1,500/month vs. 60% of salary).

filing_deadline_notes: Must commence within 24 hours after performing work-related activity
notes: NOTE: Georgia has no workers' compensation presumption for this condition. Cancer coverage (§ 25-3-23) is an employer insurance mandate; cardiovascular coverage (§ 45-9-85) is the State Indemnification Fund lump-sum disability/death benefit; PTSD coverage (§§ 45-25-1 et seq.) is a mandatory employer-funded insurance benefit. None is a WC presumption shifting the burden of proof. Presumption applies if heart attack, stroke, or vascular rupture: commenced while performing work-related activity, while on duty after such activity, or not later than 24 hours after such activity; AND directly or proximately resulted in death or disability. Rebuttable by competent medical evidence that it was not related to work activity or was caused solely by cardiovascular disease risk factors.

condition_specific: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD); employer-funded insurance benefit
notes: Georgia has no workers' compensation presumption for this condition. Cancer coverage (§ 25-3-23) is an employer insurance mandate; cardiovascular coverage (§ 45-9-85) is a lump-sum disability/death benefit through the State Indemnification Fund; and PTSD coverage (§§ 45-25-1 et seq., the Ashley Wilson Act) is a mandatory employer-funded insurance benefit. None of these shifts the burden of proof the way a true workers' compensation presumption would. The Ashley Wilson Act (HB 451) was signed May 1, 2024, with claims eligible starting January 1, 2025. Benefits: a $3,000 lump sum on diagnosis, plus 60% of monthly salary (up to $5,000/month for paid staff, $1,500/month for volunteers) for up to 36 months. PTSD must be diagnosed by a licensed mental health professional within 2 years of a qualifying traumatic event occurring on or after July 1, 2024. Covered groups include peace officers, firefighters, emergency medical professionals, 911 operators, probation officers, and jail and correctional officers. The employer must provide this insurance coverage.
